property_summary: Calling version() always returns the string "1.0.0".
After setL1BlockValues, number equals the _number parameter.
After the depositor calls setL1BlockValues, the state variable number must equal the provided _number parameter.
After setL1BlockValues is called, the timestamp state variable equals the _timestamp argument passed in the call.
After setL1BlockValues is called, the timestamp state variable must not be zero when _timestamp is non-zero.
After setL1BlockValues completes, the stored basefee equals the _basefee argument passed in the function call.
After setL1BlockValues completes, the stored basefee equals the most recently passed _basefee argument.
After setL1BlockValues, the stored basefee equals the _basefee argument that was passed, unless an even-numbered call was made after an odd-numbered one with a different _basefee.
After any two consecutive calls to setL1BlockValues with different _basefee arguments, the stored basefee changes.
After a call to setL1BlockValues, the stored basefee is always equal to the _basefee argument passed in that call.
After a call to setL1BlockValues with non-zero _basefee, the public state variable basefee must equal the supplied _basefee.
After calling setL1BlockValues with a non-depositor account, basefee remains unchanged (zero).
After calling setL1BlockValues() from a non-depositor account, all state variables that would be written by a successful call remain unchanged (their values before the call).
When caller is not the depositor, basefee remains unchanged after calling setL1BlockValues.
After calling setL1BlockValues from any account other than the depositor, basefee remains unchanged (equal to zero, which is the initial value before any successful call).
After calling setL1BlockValues from any account, basefee equals the value passed as the _basefee parameter.
The hash state variable after setL1BlockValues always equals the _hash argument passed to the function.
After calling setL1BlockValues, the public getter hash() returns a non-zero value.
After calling setL1BlockValues with arbitrary parameters, the hash state variable should equal the _hash parameter passed.
At the end of a setL1BlockValues call, the public getter c.hash() matches the fifth fuzz argument (a bytes32) no matter what the other arguments are.
After setL1BlockValues, the hash state variable equals the _hash argument passed.
After calling setL1BlockValues, sequenceNumber equals the _sequenceNumber argument provided in the call
After calling setL1BlockValues, the value of batcherHash should equal the _batcherHash argument passed in.
After calling setL1BlockValues, batcherHash is unchanged from its previous value.
After setL1BlockValues, the number field must not be overwritten by a value based on _batcherHash, i.e., number must equal the _number argument passed in.
After calling setL1BlockValues, the value of l1FeeOverhead must equal the _l1FeeOverhead argument passed in.
After calling setL1BlockValues, the value of number must equal the _number argument, because the bug overwrites number with a truncated _batcherHash.
After a call to setL1BlockValues, the batcherHash state variable equals the _batcherHash argument passed.
When calling setL1BlockValues, the batcherHash state variable must be set to the value of the last call's _batcherHash argument.
After setL1BlockValues, batcherHash must equal the passed _batcherHash parameter.
After setL1BlockValues, batcherHash must equal the keccak256 hash of the _batcherHash parameter padded to 32 bytes.
After calling setL1BlockValues, the stored batcherHash is equal to the provided _batcherHash parameter.
After setL1BlockValues, the stored batcherHash should be equal to the keccak256 hash of the uint256 parameter _batcherHash padded to 32 bytes.
After calling setL1BlockValues, the stored batcherHash is equal to the provided _batcherHash parameter.
After calling setL1BlockValues with arbitrary parameters, the public state variable l1FeeOverhead equals the provided _l1FeeOverhead argument.
After setL1BlockValues is called by anyone other than the depositor, l1FeeScalar must remain unchanged (the call must revert).
The setL1BlockValues function should revert when called by any address other than DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT.
After calling setL1BlockValues, the value of l1FeeScalar should equal the provided _l1FeeScalar parameter.
setL1BlockValues reverts when caller is not the constant depositor account defined in the contract.
